newsitem.title: KENYA: Burundi denies army massacred people in church.
newsitem.headline: Burundi denies army massacred people in church.

text.p: Burundi has rejected claims by Amnesty International that its Tutsi-led security forces have killed at least 1,000 unarmed Hutu civilians, some sheltering in churches, in the past month.
"We refute the allegations completely," Jean-Luc Ndizeye, spokesman for President Pierre Buyoya, told Reuters by telephone from the Burundian capital Bujumbura.
The London-based human rights organisation said on Friday that in the latest case, up to 500 people were massacred in the Pentecostal Church of Nyarurama on December 3.

The victims had been told that they could shelter safely in the church but, once they were inside, soldiers surrounded the building, threw grenades inside and shot at or bayoneted those trying to escape, Amnesty said in a news release.
Then the troops set the church on fire, sought out those who had escaped and killed them as well, Amnesty said.
Ndizeye said that rebel activity was prevalent in the area Amnesty International spoke of and "there have been casualties in such areas, this everyone knows".
Ndizeye also said the compilers of the Amnesty International report were well known to the Burundi government. He did not say whether they were Burundians or foreigners.
"We wonder why Amnesty persists in utilising people whose integrity is in question," Ndizeye told Reuters.
Ndizeye said the government of military ruler Buyoya had a programme of restoring complete peace in the country.
"We have a peace plan not an extermination plan. We seek peace to build, not peace to exterminate," he added.
Amnesty said: "The local people believe that places of worship offer symbolic protection. But clearly no place appears to be too sacred for the army to carry out massacres."

"What is happening in Burundi appears to be a deliberate policy of systematic extermination of a section of the population, with Buyoya presiding over more than 10,000 killings since August," Amnesty International said.
It said the army had killed at least 1,000 Hutus in four provinces since November.
